# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost cap.** `--max-tokens N` caps billed-equivalent tokens (input, output, cache read and
  cache write, unweighted). Admission is projected: until a run reports its cost only one run is
  in flight; after that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every in-flight run at the
  largest observed cost fits. Realized spend can still exceed the cap by one run's cost when a
  run's cost is larger than any seen before. The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k
  against a 450k cap; that file is kept as evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

name: receiving-code-review
description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
---

# Code Review Reception

## Overview

Code review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.

**Core principle:** Verify before implementing. Ask before assuming. Technical correctness over social comfort.

## The Response Pattern

```
WHEN receiving code review feedback:

1. READ: Complete feedback without reacting
2. UNDERSTAND: Restate requirement in own words (or ask)
3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality
4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?
5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback
6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each
```

## Forbidden Responses

**NEVER:**
- "You're absolutely right!" (explicit instruction-file violation)
- "Great point!" / "Excellent feedback!" (performative)
- "Let me implement that now" (before verification)

**INSTEAD:**
- Restate the technical requirement
- Ask clarifying questions
- Push back with technical reasoning if wrong
- Just start working (actions > words)

## Handling Unclear Feedback

```
IF any item is unclear:
  STOP - do not implement anything yet
  ASK for clarification on unclear items

WHY: Items may be related. Partial understanding = wrong implementation.
```

**Example:**
```
your human partner: "Fix 1-6"
You understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.

❌ WRONG: Implement 1,2,3,6 now, ask about 4,5 later
✅ RIGHT: "I understand items 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before proceeding."
```

## Source-Specific Handling

### From your human partner
- **Trusted** - implement after understanding
- **Still ask** if scope unclear
- **No performative agreement**
- **Skip to action** or technical acknowledgment

### From External Reviewers
```
BEFORE implementing:
  1. Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase?
  2. Check: Breaks existing functionality?
  3. Check: Reason for current implementation?
  4. Check: Works on all platforms/versions?
  5. Check: Does reviewer understand full context?

IF suggestion seems wrong:
  Push back with technical reasoning

IF can't easily verify:
  Say so: "I can't verify this without [X]. Should I [investigate/ask/proceed]?"

IF conflicts with your human partner's prior decisions:
  Stop and discuss with your human partner first
```

**your human partner's rule:** "External feedback - be skeptical, but check carefully"

## YAGNI Check for "Professional" Features

```
IF reviewer suggests "implementing properly":
  grep codebase for actual usage

  IF unused: "This endpoint isn't called. Remove it (YAGNI)?"
  IF used: Then implement properly
```

**your human partner's rule:** "You and reviewer both report to me. If we don't need this feature, don't add it."

## Implementation Order

```
FOR multi-item feedback:
  1. Clarify anything unclear FIRST
  2. Then implement in this order:
     - Blocking issues (breaks, security)
     - Simple fixes (typos, imports)
     - Complex fixes (refactoring, logic)
  3. Test each fix individually
  4. Verify no regressions
```

## When To Push Back

Push back when:
- Suggestion breaks existing functionality
- Reviewer lacks full context
- Violates YAGNI (unused feature)
- Technically incorrect for this stack
- Legacy/compatibility reasons exist
- Conflicts with your human partner's architectural decisions

**How to push back:**
- Use technical reasoning, not defensiveness
- Ask specific questions
- Reference working tests/code
- Involve your human partner if architectural

**If you're uncomfortable pushing back out loud:** Name that tension, then tell your partner about the issue you've seen. They'll appreciate your honesty.

## Acknowledging Correct Feedback

When feedback IS correct:
```
✅ "Fixed. [Brief description of what changed]"
✅ "Good catch - [specific issue]. Fixed in [location]."
✅ [Just fix it and show in the code]

❌ "You're absolutely right!"
❌ "Great point!"
❌ "Thanks for catching that!"
❌ "Thanks for [anything]"
❌ ANY gratitude expression
```

**Why no thanks:** Actions speak. Just fix it. The code itself shows you heard the feedback.

**If you catch yourself about to write "Thanks":** DELETE IT. State the fix instead.

## Gracefully Correcting Your Pushback

If you pushed back and were wrong:
```
✅ "You were right - I checked [X] and it does [Y]. Implementing now."
✅ "Verified this and you're correct. My initial understanding was wrong because [reason]. Fixing."

❌ Long apology
❌ Defending why you pushed back
❌ Over-explaining
```

State the correction factually and move on.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Performative agreement | State requirement or just act |
| Blind implementation | Verify against codebase first |
| Batch without testing | One at a time, test each |
| Assuming reviewer is right | Check if breaks things |
| Avoiding pushback | Technical correctness > comfort |
| Partial implementation | Clarify all items first |
| Can't verify, proceed anyway | State limitation, ask for direction |

## Real Examples

**Performative Agreement (Bad):**
```
Reviewer: "Remove legacy code"
❌ "You're absolutely right! Let me remove that..."
```

**Technical Verification (Good):**
```
Reviewer: "Remove legacy code"
✅ "Checking... build target is 10.15+, this API needs 13+. Need legacy for backward compat. Current impl has wrong bundle ID - fix it or drop pre-13 support?"
```

**YAGNI (Good):**
```
Reviewer: "Implement proper metrics tracking with database, date filters, CSV export"
✅ "Grepped codebase - nothing calls this endpoint. Remove it (YAGNI)? Or is there usage I'm missing?"
```

**Unclear Item (Good):**
```
your human partner: "Fix items 1-6"
You understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.
✅ "Understand 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before implementing."
```

## GitHub Thread Replies

When replying to inline review comments on GitHub, reply in the comment thread (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{id}/replies`), not as a top-level PR comment.

# Requesting Code Review

Dispatch a code reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade. The reviewer gets precisely crafted context for evaluation — never your session's history.

**Core principle:** Review early, review often.

## When to Request Review

**Mandatory:**
- After each task in subagent-driven development
- After completing major feature
- Before merge to main

**Optional but valuable:**
- When stuck (fresh perspective)
- Before refactoring (baseline check)
- After fixing complex bug

## How to Request

**1. Get git SHAs:**
```bash
BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or: git merge-base origin/main HEAD
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

**2. Dispatch code reviewer subagent:**

Dispatch a `general-purpose` subagent, filling the template at [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)

**Placeholders:**
- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary of what you built
- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit

**3. Act on feedback:**
- Fix Critical issues immediately
- Fix Important issues before proceeding
- Note Minor issues for later
- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)

## Example

```
[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]

You: Let me request code review before proceeding.

BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1)
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

[Dispatch code reviewer subagent]
  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types
  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/superpowers/plans/deployment-plan.md
  BASE_SHA: a7981ec
  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661

[Subagent returns]:
  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
  Issues:
    Important: Missing progress indicators
    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
  Assessment: Ready to proceed

You: [Fix progress indicators]
[Continue to Task 3]
```

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "I'll just review the diff myself instead of dispatching a reviewer" | You're the coordinator — reviewing the diff inline burns the context window you need to keep driving the work. Dispatch a reviewer subagent: the diff and the evaluation live in its context, and only the findings come back to you. |
| "The reviewer needs my whole session history to understand the change" | Hand it precisely crafted context, never your session's history. That keeps the reviewer on the work product, not your thought process. |

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip review because "it's simple"
- Ignore Critical issues
- Proceed with unfixed Important issues
- Argue with valid technical feedback

**If reviewer wrong:**
- Push back with technical reasoning
- Show code/tests that prove it works
- Request clarification

See template at: [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)

3|description: Regression testing strategies for AI-assisted development. Sandbox-mode API testing without database dependencies, automated bug-check workflows, and patterns to catch AI blind spots where the same model writes and reviews code. Use when adding regression coverage to AI-assisted code, or when the same model both wrote and reviewed a change.

6|---
7|
8|# AI Regression Testing
9|
10|Testing patterns specifically designed for AI-assisted development, where the same model writes code and reviews it — creating systematic blind spots that only automated tests can catch.
11|
12|## When to Activate
13|
14|- AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) has modified API routes or backend logic
15|- A bug was found and fixed — need to prevent re-introduction
16|- Project has a sandbox/mock mode that can be leveraged for DB-free testing
17|- Running `/bug-check` or similar review commands after code changes
18|- Multiple code paths exist (sandbox vs production, feature flags, etc.)
19|
20|## The Core Problem
21|
22|When an AI writes code and then reviews its own work, it carries the same assumptions into both steps. This creates a predictable failure pattern:
23|
24|```
25|AI writes fix → AI reviews fix → AI says "looks correct" → Bug still exists
26|```
27|
28|**Real-world example** (observed in production):
29|
30|```
31|Fix 1: Added notification_settings to API response
32|  → Forgot to add it to the SELECT query
33|  → AI reviewed and missed it (same blind spot)
34|
35|Fix 2: Added it to SELECT query
36|  → TypeScript build error (column not in generated types)
37|  → AI reviewed Fix 1 but didn't catch the SELECT issue
38|
39|Fix 3: Changed to SELECT *
40|  → Fixed production path, forgot sandbox path
41|  → AI reviewed and missed it AGAIN (4th occurrence)
42|
43|Fix 4: Test caught it instantly on first run PASS:
44|```
45|
46|The pattern: **sandbox/production path inconsistency** is the #1 AI-introduced regression.
47|
48|## Sandbox-Mode API Testing
49|
50|Most projects with AI-friendly architecture have a sandbox/mock mode. This is the key to fast, DB-free API testing.
51|
52|### Setup (Vitest + Next.js App Router)
53|
54|```typescript
55|// vitest.config.ts
56|import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";
57|import path from "path";
58|
59|export default defineConfig({
60|  test: {
61|    environment: "node",
62|    globals: true,
63|    include: ["__tests__/**/*.test.ts"],
64|    setupFiles: ["__tests__/setup.ts"],
65|  },
66|  resolve: {
67|    alias: {
68|      "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "."),
69|    },
70|  },
71|});
72|```
73|
74|```typescript
75|// __tests__/setup.ts
76|// Force sandbox mode — no database needed
77|process.env.SANDBOX_MODE = "true";
78|process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL = "";
79|process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = "";
80|```
81|
82|### Test Helper for Next.js API Routes
83|
84|```typescript
85|// __tests__/helpers.ts
86|import { NextRequest } from "next/server";
87|
88|export function createTestRequest(
89|  url: string,
90|  options?: {
91|    method?: string;
92|    body?: Record<string, unknown>;
93|    headers?: Record<string, string>;
94|    sandboxUserId?: string;
95|  },
96|): NextRequest {
97|  const { method = "GET", body, headers = {}, sandboxUserId } = options || {};
98|  const fullUrl = url.startsWith("http") ? url : `http://localhost:3000${url}`;
99|  const reqHeaders: Record<string, string> = { ...headers };
100|
101|  if (sandboxUserId) {
102|    reqHeaders["x-sandbox-user-id"] = sandboxUserId;
103|  }
104|
105|  const init: { method: string; headers: Record<string, string>; body?: string } = {
106|    method,
107|    headers: reqHeaders,
108|  };
109|
110|  if (body) {
111|    init.body = JSON.stringify(body);
112|    reqHeaders["content-type"] = "application/json";
113|  }
114|
115|  return new NextRequest(fullUrl, init);
116|}
117|
118|export async function parseResponse(response: Response) {
119|  const json = await response.json();
120|  return { status: response.status, json };
121|}
122|```
123|
124|### Writing Regression Tests
125|
126|The key principle: **write tests for bugs that were found, not for code that works**.
127|
128|```typescript
129|// __tests__/api/user/profile.test.ts
130|import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
131|import { createTestRequest, parseResponse } from "../../helpers";
132|import { GET, PATCH } from "@/app/api/user/profile/route";
133|
134|// Define the contract — what fields MUST be in the response
135|const REQUIRED_FIELDS = [
136|  "id",
137|  "email",
138|  "full_name",
139|  "phone",
140|  "role",
141|  "created_at",
142|  "avatar_url",
143|  "notification_settings",  // ← Added after bug found it missing
144|];
145|
146|describe("GET /api/user/profile", () => {
147|  it("returns all required fields", async () => {
148|    const req = createTestRequest("/api/user/profile");
149|    const res = await GET(req);
150|    const { status, json } = await parseResponse(res);
151|
152|    expect(status).toBe(200);
153|    for (const field of REQUIRED_FIELDS) {
154|      expect(json.data).toHaveProperty(field);
155|    }
156|  });
157|
158|  // Regression test — this exact bug was introduced by AI 4 times
159|  it("notification_settings is not undefined (BUG-R1 regression)", async () => {
160|    const req = createTestRequest("/api/user/profile");
161|    const res = await GET(req);
162|    const { json } = await parseResponse(res);
163|
164|    expect("notification_settings" in json.data).toBe(true);
165|    const ns = json.data.notification_settings;
166|    expect(ns === null || typeof ns === "object").toBe(true);
167|  });
168|});
169|```
170|
171|### Testing Sandbox/Production Parity
172|
173|The most common AI regression: fixing production path but forgetting sandbox path (or vice versa).
174|
175|```typescript
176|// Test that sandbox responses match the expected contract
177|describe("GET /api/user/messages (conversation list)", () => {
178|  it("includes partner_name in sandbox mode", async () => {
179|    const req = createTestRequest("/api/user/messages", {
180|      sandboxUserId: "user-001",
181|    });
182|    const res = await GET(req);
183|    const { json } = await parseResponse(res);
184|
185|    // This caught a bug where partner_name was added
186|    // to production path but not sandbox path
187|    if (json.data.length > 0) {
188|      for (const conv of json.data) {
189|        expect("partner_name" in conv).toBe(true);
190|      }
191|    }
192|  });
193|});
194|```
195|
196|## Integrating Tests into Bug-Check Workflow
197|
198|### Custom Command Definition
199|
200|```markdown
201|<!-- .claude/commands/bug-check.md -->
202|# Bug Check
203|
204|## Step 1: Automated Tests (mandatory, cannot skip)
205|
206|Run these commands FIRST before any code review:
207|
208|    npm run test       # Vitest test suite
209|    npm run build      # TypeScript type check + build
210|
211|- If tests fail → report as highest priority bug
212|- If build fails → report type errors as highest priority
213|- Only proceed to Step 2 if both pass
214|
215|## Step 2: Code Review (AI review)
216|
217|1. Sandbox / production path consistency
218|2. API response shape matches frontend expectations
219|3. SELECT clause completeness
220|4. Error handling with rollback
221|5. Optimistic update race conditions
222|
223|## Step 3: For each bug fixed, propose a regression test
224|```
225|
226|### The Workflow
227|
228|```
229|User: "バグチェックして" (or "/bug-check")
230|  │
231|  ├─ Step 1: npm run test
232|  │   ├─ FAIL → Bug found mechanically (no AI judgment needed)
233|  │   └─ PASS → Continue
234|  │
235|  ├─ Step 2: npm run build
236|  │   ├─ FAIL → Type error found mechanically
237|  │   └─ PASS → Continue
238|  │
239|  ├─ Step 3: AI code review (with known blind spots in mind)
240|  │   └─ Findings reported
241|  │
242|  └─ Step 4: For each fix, write a regression test
243|      └─ Next bug-check catches if fix breaks
244|```
245|
246|## Common AI Regression Patterns
247|
248|### Pattern 1: Sandbox/Production Path Mismatch
249|
250|**Frequency**: Most common (observed in 3 out of 4 regressions)
251|
252|```typescript
253|// FAIL: AI adds field to production path only
254|if (isSandboxMode()) {
255|  return { data: { id, email, name } };  // Missing new field
256|}
257|// Production path
258|return { data: { id, email, name, notification_settings } };
259|
260|// PASS: Both paths must return the same shape
261|if (isSandboxMode()) {
262|  return { data: { id, email, name, notification_settings: null } };
263|}
264|return { data: { id, email, name, notification_settings } };
265|```
266|
267|**Test to catch it**:
268|
269|```typescript
270|it("sandbox and production return same fields", async () => {
271|  // In test env, sandbox mode is forced ON
272|  const res = await GET(createTestRequest("/api/user/profile"));
273|  const { json } = await parseResponse(res);
274|
275|  for (const field of REQUIRED_FIELDS) {
276|    expect(json.data).toHaveProperty(field);
277|  }
278|});
279|```
280|
281|### Pattern 2: SELECT Clause Omission
282|
283|**Frequency**: Common with Supabase/Prisma when adding new columns
284|
285|```typescript
286|// FAIL: New column added to response but not to SELECT
287|const { data } = await supabase
288|  .from("users")
289|  .select("id, email, name")  // notification_settings not here
290|  .single();
291|
292|return { data: { ...data, notification_settings: data.notification_settings } };
293|// → notification_settings is always undefined
294|
295|// PASS: Use SELECT * or explicitly include new columns
296|const { data } = await supabase
297|  .from("users")
298|  .select("*")
299|  .single();
300|```
301|
302|### Pattern 3: Error State Leakage
303|
304|**Frequency**: Moderate — when adding error handling to existing components
305|
306|```typescript
307|// FAIL: Error state set but old data not cleared
308|catch (err) {
309|  setError("Failed to load");
310|  // reservations still shows data from previous tab!
311|}
312|
313|// PASS: Clear related state on error
314|catch (err) {
315|  setReservations([]);  // Clear stale data
316|  setError("Failed to load");
317|}
318|```
319|
320|### Pattern 4: Optimistic Update Without Proper Rollback
321|
322|```typescript
323|// FAIL: No rollback on failure
324|const handleRemove = async (id: string) => {
325|  setItems(prev => prev.filter(i => i.id !== id));
326|  await fetch(`/api/items/${id}`, { method: "DELETE" });
327|  // If API fails, item is gone from UI but still in DB
328|};
329|
330|// PASS: Capture previous state and rollback on failure
331|const handleRemove = async (id: string) => {
332|  const prevItems = [...items];
333|  setItems(prev => prev.filter(i => i.id !== id));
334|  try {
335|    const res = await fetch(`/api/items/${id}`, { method: "DELETE" });
336|    if (!res.ok) throw new Error("API error");
337|  } catch {
338|    setItems(prevItems);  // Rollback
339|    alert("削除に失敗しました");
340|  }
341|};
342|```
343|
344|## Strategy: Test Where Bugs Were Found
345|
346|Don't aim for 100% coverage. Instead:
347|
348|```
349|Bug found in /api/user/profile     → Write test for profile API
350|Bug found in /api/user/messages    → Write test for messages API
351|Bug found in /api/user/favorites   → Write test for favorites API
352|No bug in /api/user/notifications  → Don't write test (yet)
353|```
354|
355|**Why this works with AI development:**
356|
357|1. AI tends to make the **same category of mistake** repeatedly
358|2. Bugs cluster in complex areas (auth, multi-path logic, state management)
359|3. Once tested, that exact regression **cannot happen again**
360|4. Test count grows organically with bug fixes — no wasted effort
361|
362|## Quick Reference
363|
364|| AI Regression Pattern | Test Strategy | Priority |
365||---|---|---|
366|| Sandbox/production mismatch | Assert same response shape in sandbox mode |  High |
367|| SELECT clause omission | Assert all required fields in response |  High |
368|| Error state leakage | Assert state cleanup on error |  Medium |
369|| Missing rollback | Assert state restored on API failure |  Medium |
370|| Type cast masking null | Assert field is not undefined |  Medium |
371|
372|## DO / DON'T
373|
374|**DO:**
375|- Write tests immediately after finding a bug (before fixing it if possible)
376|- Test the API response shape, not the implementation

"""Paired agent evaluation: the same agent and model fix executable bugs with and without OXIDE.

    uv run --with pyarrow python scripts/agent_eval fetch PARQUET   # once: pinned dataset rows
    uv run python scripts/agent_eval verify [--jobs 4]              # tasks whose tests run here
    uv run python scripts/agent_eval run --model M [--tasks 20 --reps 3 --jobs 4]
    uv run python scripts/agent_eval report RESULTS.jsonl

Protocol and the pass/fail rule are in ``fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md``; fix them before
reading results. Arms differ in one thing: the ``oxide mcp`` tool (and one sentence naming it).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import diagnose
import report
import run
import tasks


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    fetch = commands.add_parser("fetch", help="narrow the dataset parquet to buildable repos")
    fetch.add_argument("parquet", type=Path)
    fetch.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=tasks.CACHE / "candidates.json")
    verify = commands.add_parser("verify", help="keep instances whose gold patch passes here")
    verify.add_argument("--candidates", type=Path, default=tasks.CACHE / "candidates.json")
    verify.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=4)
    verify.add_argument("--only", action="append", default=[], help="instance id (repeatable)")
    go = commands.add_parser("run", help="run every task in every arm")
    go.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="provider/model, e.g. openai/gpt-6-luna")
    go.add_argument("--runner", choices=run.RUNNERS, default="opencode", help="agent CLI to drive")
    go.add_argument("--tasks", type=int, default=20, help="first N tasks in the predeclared order")
    go.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=3)
    go.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=4)
    go.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=1200, help="seconds per agent run")
    go.add_argument("--arms", nargs="+", choices=run.ARM_NAMES, default=list(run.ARMS))
    go.add_argument("--base-src", type=Path, default=None, help="oxide-base: snapshot of src/oxide")
    go.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
    go.add_argument("--only", action="append", default=[], help="instance id (repeatable)")
    go.add_argument("--split", choices=("dev", "heldout"), default="dev")
    go.add_argument(
        "--max-tokens", type=int, default=None, help="start no run once this much is spent"
    )
    go.add_argument("--final", action="store_true", help="open a held-out set: one look per set")
    summary = commands.add_parser("report", help="paired comparison of a results file")
    summary.add_argument("results", type=Path)
    summary.add_argument("--test", default="oxide", choices=run.ARM_NAMES)
    summary.add_argument("--reference", default="control", choices=run.ARM_NAMES)
    diag = commands.add_parser("diagnose", help="classify OXIDE-arm runs from retained traces")
    diag.add_argument("results", type=Path)
    diag.add_argument("--arm", default="oxide", choices=run.ARM_NAMES)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "fetch":
        tasks.fetch(args.parquet, args.out)
    elif args.command == "verify":
        tasks.verify(args.candidates, args.jobs, args.only)
    elif args.command == "run":
        run.run_all(args)
    elif args.command == "report":
        report.report(args.results, args.test, args.reference)
    else:
        print(diagnose.diagnose(args.results, args.arm))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1:"""Protocol guards for the paired agent evaluation: what a results file is bound to, how much
2:it may spend, and how often a held-out task set may be opened.
3:
4:Pure functions only, so the rules are tested without running an agent.
5:"""
6:
7:from __future__ import annotations
8:
9:import hashlib
10:import json
11:from pathlib import Path
12:from typing import Any
13:
14:PROTOCOL = "agent-swe-v2"
15:
16:
17:def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
18:    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
19:
20:
21:def spend(tokens: dict[str, int]) -> int:
22:    """Tokens billed for one run, unweighted: every input, output and cache token. Prices vary
23:    by provider and cache tier, so the cap is in tokens; USD is the token counts times a price
24:    the operator applies to the recorded counts."""
25:    return sum(tokens.get(k, 0) for k in ("input", "output", "cache_read", "cache_write"))
26:
27:
28:def row_has_spend(row: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
29:    return "spend" in row or isinstance(row.get("tokens"), dict)
30:
31:
32:def row_spend(row: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
33:    """A recorded run's spend: the stored figure, or its tokens for rows written before it."""
34:    if "spend" in row:
35:        return int(row["spend"])
36:    return spend(row["tokens"]) if isinstance(row.get("tokens"), dict) else 0
37:
38:
39:def spent(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
40:    return sum(row_spend(r) for r in rows)
41:
42:
43:def admit(spent_so_far: int, in_flight: int, observed_max: int | None, cap: int | None) -> bool:
44:    """Whether one more run may start under the token cap.
45:
46:    Before any run has reported its spend there is nothing to project from, so one run at a
47:    time calibrates the cost. After that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every
48:    in-flight run and this one, each at the largest observed run cost, still fits the cap.
49:    A start-time check alone let a first wave of parallel runs overshoot a cap ~1.8x."""
50:    if cap is None:
51:        return True
52:    if observed_max is None:
53:        return in_flight == 0 and spent_so_far < cap
54:    return spent_so_far + (in_flight + 1) * observed_max <= cap
55:
56:
57:def check_manifest(path: Path, manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
58:    """Write the manifest beside a new results file, or refuse to resume under a different one.
59:
60:    A results file is only comparable to runs made under the same tasks, code, prompt, arm
61:    configuration and agent binary. Resuming under a changed protocol mixes two experiments."""
62:    if not path.exists():
63:        path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
64:        return
65:    recorded = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
66:    diff = sorted(k for k in set(recorded) | set(manifest) if recorded.get(k) != manifest.get(k))
67:    if diff:
68:        raise SystemExit(
69:            f"{path} was recorded under a different protocol ({', '.join(diff)} changed); "
70:            "start a new results file instead of resuming"
71:        )
72:
73:
74:def heldout_open(log: Path, tasks_sha: str, out: Path) -> None:
75:    """A held-out task set is opened once. Resuming the same results file is allowed; a second
76:    file on the same set is a second look, which the protocol forbids."""
77:    entries = [json.loads(line) for line in log.read_text().splitlines()] if log.exists() else []
78:    for entry in entries:
79:        if entry["tasks_sha256"] == tasks_sha and entry["out"] != str(out):
80:            raise SystemExit(
81:                f"held-out tasks {tasks_sha[:12]} were already opened by {entry['out']}; "
82:                "a held-out set is one look, so write a new held-out set instead"
83:            )
84:    if not any(e["tasks_sha256"] == tasks_sha and e["out"] == str(out) for e in entries):
85:        with log.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
86:            file.write(json.dumps({"tasks_sha256": tasks_sha, "out": str(out)}) + "\n")

2:
3:    uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py      # from the repository root
4:    # equivalent: cd scripts/agent_eval && uv run python -m heldout
5:
6:Writes ``fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json`` (kept tasks) and
7:``fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-rejections.json`` (every PR the search returned, with a reason).

"""Held-out agent-eval tasks: pull requests merged on or after ``CUTOFF``, in the tasks.json schema.

    uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py      # from the repository root
    # equivalent: cd scripts/agent_eval && uv run python -m heldout

Writes ``fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json`` (kept tasks) and
``fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-rejections.json`` (every PR the search returned, with a reason).
Run it under ``systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=200% -p MemoryMax=3G`` for the builds.

Selection, frozen with ``CUTOFF`` and ``QUOTA``:
  a. merged at or after ``CUTOFF`` (UTC), found by ``gh pr list --search merged:>=CUTOFF``;
  b. exactly one linked issue (GitHub ``closingIssuesReferences``: closing keywords or a manual
     link) whose body is non-empty; the problem text is its title and body;
  c. the diff touches a ``.py`` file under the repo's test dir (``REPOS``; ``tests/`` where
     ``REPOS`` gives none) and a non-test ``.py`` file;
  d. fail-to-pass non-empty: tests run before and after the gold patch in a fresh environment
     (``tasks.checkout``/``environment``/``apply``/``tests``). A PR is kept only if a second,
     independent measurement confirms every fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after,
     with the rule of ``tasks.verify_one``. Its pass-to-pass set (tests passing before and after)
     must be non-empty: otherwise "pass-to-pass empty after intersection" (added after run 2).
Screened PRs are processed in ``tasks.order`` (sha256 of the id); the first ``QUOTA`` that pass
are kept, two environment builds at a time. Candidates after the quota are recorded, not run.

tests are verified with that recipe. The frozen ``REPOS`` recipe (Python 3.9, setuptools<70)
cannot build PRs merged after the cutoff: flask now requires Python >= 3.10, and setuptools<70
rejects PEP 639 string licenses. Dev tasks in tasks.json keep the frozen ``REPOS`` recipe.

# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost cap.** `--max-tokens N` caps billed-equivalent tokens (input, output, cache read and
  cache write, unweighted). Admission is projected: until a run reports its cost only one run is
  in flight; after that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every in-flight run at the
  largest observed cost fits. Realized spend can still exceed the cap by one run's cost when a
  run's cost is larger than any seen before. The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k
  against a 450k cap; that file is kept as evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

## Commands

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

"""Paired comparison: per-task resolve rate in each arm, bootstrap interval over tasks."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import statistics
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any

BOOTSTRAP = 10_000


def interval(diffs: list[float]) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """95% percentile bootstrap of the mean paired difference, resampling tasks."""
    rng = random.Random(0)
    means = sorted(statistics.fmean(rng.choices(diffs, k=len(diffs))) for _ in range(BOOTSTRAP))
    return means[int(0.025 * BOOTSTRAP)], means[int(0.975 * BOOTSTRAP) - 1]


def plan_block(
    path: Path, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], scored: list[dict[str, Any]]
) -> str | None:
    """None when nothing was planned, or every planned task, arm, and repetition is scored."""
    side = path.with_name(path.stem + ".manifest.json")
    if not side.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        manifest = json.loads(side.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return "invalid: unreadable manifest"
    if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
        return "invalid: unreadable manifest"
    arms = manifest.get("arms")
    tasks_n = manifest.get("tasks")
    reps = manifest.get("reps")
    if (
        not isinstance(arms, list)
        or not arms
        or not isinstance(tasks_n, int)
        or isinstance(tasks_n, bool)
        or tasks_n < 0
        or not isinstance(reps, int)
        or isinstance(reps, bool)
        or reps < 1
        or any(not isinstance(arm, str) or not arm for arm in arms)
    ):
        return "invalid: manifest missing tasks, arms, or reps"
    planned = [arm for arm in arms if isinstance(arm, str)]
    task_ids = {row["task"] for row in rows}
    scored_keys = {(row["task"], row["arm"], row["rep"]) for row in scored}
    total = tasks_n * len(planned) * reps
    got = sum(
        1
        for _task, arm, rep in scored_keys
        if arm in planned
        and isinstance(rep, int)
        and not isinstance(rep, bool)
        and 0 <= rep < reps
    )
    # shortcut: same-size task swap still passes, upgrade when manifest lists ids
    if len(task_ids) == tasks_n and got == total:
        return None
    return f"provisional: incomplete planned matrix ({got}/{total} scored)"


def report(path: Path, test: str = "oxide", reference: str = "control") -> None:
    attempts = [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines()]
    rows = list({(r["task"], r["arm"], r["rep"]): r for r in attempts}.values())
    errors = [
        r for r in rows if r["resolved"] is None or r.get("status") not in (None, "ok", "timeout")
    ]
    scored = [r for r in rows if r not in errors]
    rate: dict[str, dict[str, list[bool]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for r in scored:
        rate[r["task"]][r["arm"]].append(bool(r["resolved"]))
    both = {t: arms for t, arms in rate.items() if arms[test] and arms[reference]}
    diffs = [statistics.fmean(a[test]) - statistics.fmean(a[reference]) for a in both.values()]
    print(f"{len(scored)} scored runs, {len(errors)} harness errors, {len(both)} paired tasks")
    if any("provider.auth:" in str(r.get("error", "")) for r in errors):
        print("verdict: invalid: provider authentication failure")
        return
    if rows and len(errors) / len(rows) > 0.10:
        print("verdict: invalid: more than 10% harness errors")
        return
    blocked = plan_block(path, rows, scored)
    if blocked and not blocked.startswith("provisional:"):
        print("verdict:", blocked)
        return
    if not diffs:
        print("verdict:", blocked or "no paired tasks")
        return
    for arm in (reference, test):
        runs = [r for r in scored if r["arm"] == arm]
        print(
            f"{arm:12} resolved {sum(r['resolved'] for r in runs)}/{len(runs)}"
            f"  median seconds {statistics.median(r['seconds'] for r in runs):.0f}"
            f"  median output tokens {statistics.median(r['tokens']['output'] for r in runs):.0f}"
            f"  median steps {statistics.median(r['steps'] for r in runs):.0f}"
        )
    test_runs = [r for r in scored if r["arm"] == test]
    used = sum(any(k.startswith("oxide") for k in r["calls"]) for r in test_runs)
    print(
        f"oxide tool used in {used}/{len(test_runs)} {test} runs; "
        f"median index {statistics.median(r.get('index_seconds', 0) for r in test_runs):.1f} s"
    )
    low, high = interval(diffs)
    better, worse = sum(d > 0 for d in diffs), sum(d < 0 for d in diffs)
    print(
        f"paired resolve-rate difference ({test} - {reference}): {statistics.fmean(diffs):+.3f}"
        f"  95% CI [{low:+.3f}, {high:+.3f}]  tasks better/worse/tied "
        f"{better}/{worse}/{len(diffs) - better - worse}"
    )
    if blocked:
        print("verdict:", blocked)
        return
    verdict = f"{test} improves task success" if low > 0 else "no demonstrated improvement"
    print("verdict:", verdict)

"""Final report verdicts require the planned task/arm/repetition matrix to be scored."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Any

SCRIPTS = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "agent_eval")
if SCRIPTS not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPTS)

report_mod: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("report")


def _row(task: str, arm: str, rep: int, *, resolved: bool | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    row: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task": task,
        "arm": arm,
        "rep": rep,
        "resolved": resolved,
        "seconds": 1,
        "tokens": {"output": 1},
        "steps": 1,
        "calls": {},
        "status": "ok" if resolved is not None else "harness-error",
    }
    if resolved is None:
        row["error"] = "boom"
    return row


def _write(
    tmp_path: Path, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], manifest: dict[str, Any] | None
) -> Path:
    results = tmp_path / "results.jsonl"
    results.write_text("".join(json.dumps(row) + "\n" for row in rows), encoding="utf-8")
    if manifest is not None:
        side = results.with_name(results.stem + ".manifest.json")
        side.write_text(json.dumps(manifest), encoding="utf-8")
    return results


def _winning_pair() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [
        _row("only", "control", 0, resolved=False),
        _row("only", "oxide", 0, resolved=True),
    ]


def test_incomplete_plan_is_provisional_not_a_success(tmp_path: Path, capsys: Any) -> None:
    # The review reproduction: 20 tasks × 3 reps, one scored rep per arm, oxide wins.
    manifest = {"tasks": 20, "reps": 3, "arms": ["control", "oxide"]}
    report_mod.report(_write(tmp_path, _winning_pair(), manifest))
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "verdict: provisional: incomplete planned matrix (2/120 scored)" in out
    assert "improves task success" not in out
    assert "no demonstrated improvement" not in out


def test_scored_error_cell_blocks_a_final_verdict(tmp_path: Path, capsys: Any) -> None:
    # 1/10 errors does not trip the 10% rule, but that cell was planned.
    rows = [
        _row(str(task), arm, 0, resolved=arm == "oxide")
        for task in range(4)
        for arm in ("control", "oxide")
    ]
    rows.append(_row("4", "control", 0, resolved=False))
    rows.append(_row("4", "oxide", 0, resolved=None))
    manifest = {"tasks": 5, "reps": 1, "arms": ["control", "oxide"]}
    report_mod.report(_write(tmp_path, rows, manifest))
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "verdict: provisional: incomplete planned matrix (9/10 scored)" in out
    assert "improves task success" not in out


def test_complete_manifest_and_retried_runs_keep_the_final_verdict(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: Any
) -> None:
    rows = [
        _row("only", "oxide", 0, resolved=None),
        *_winning_pair(),
    ]
    manifest = {"tasks": 1, "reps": 1, "arms": ["control", "oxide"]}
    report_mod.report(_write(tmp_path, rows, manifest))
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "verdict: oxide improves task success" in out
    assert "provisional" not in out


def test_results_without_a_manifest_keep_their_verdict(tmp_path: Path, capsys: Any) -> None:
    report_mod.report(_write(tmp_path, _winning_pair(), None))
    assert "verdict: oxide improves task success" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_unreadable_manifest_is_not_a_final_verdict(tmp_path: Path, capsys: Any) -> None:
    results = _write(tmp_path, _winning_pair(), None)
    results.with_name(results.stem + ".manifest.json").write_text("{", encoding="utf-8")
    report_mod.report(results)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "verdict: invalid: unreadable manifest" in out
    assert "improves task success" not in out

def confine_editable(argv: list[str], work: Path, venv: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Editable install under bubblewrap. ``confine`` has one writable; the venv bind is spliced
    before ``--die-with-parent`` so a setuptools hook cannot use the host."""
    wrapped = confine.confine(argv, writable=work, hide=build_hides(), net=False)
    marker = "--die-with-parent"
    try:
        at = wrapped.index(marker)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise RuntimeError("confine.confine argv has no --die-with-parent") from error
    return [*wrapped[:at], "--bind", str(venv), str(venv), *wrapped[at:]]


def environment(task: dict[str, Any], work: Path, venv: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A venv with the checkout installed editable; the env for processes that use it.
    A ``dated`` task resolves dependencies as of the issue's date. A task's ``build`` block
    (``python``, ``setuptools``) overrides the REPOS recipe; dev tasks carry none."""
    python, extra = REPOS[task["repo"]]
    build = task.get("build", {})
    python = build.get("python", python)
    setuptools = build.get("setuptools", "setuptools<70")
    env = {"SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION": task["version"], "VIRTUAL_ENV": str(venv)}
    made = sh("uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", python, venv)
    if made.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"venv: {made.stderr[-400:]}")

    def install(
        *args: str,
        era: bool = True,
        extra: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = lambda argv: argv,
    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        argv = ["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "-p", str(venv / "bin" / "python")]
        date = ["--exclude-newer", task["created_at"]] if era and task["dated"] else []
        return sh(*wrap([*argv, *date, *args]), env={**env, **(extra or {})})

    # Dev recipe: setuptools stays below 70 because old pytest and plugins import pkg_resources.
    # A held-out recipe names its own setuptools, verified with that recipe.
    # Only the editable install runs the task's build hooks, so only that command is confined.
    install(setuptools, "wheel", "setuptools_scm", "flit_core", era=False)
    install("pytest")
    for spec in (f"{work}[{extra}]", str(work)) if extra else (str(work),):
        done = install(
            "--offline",
            "--no-build-isolation",
            "-e",
            spec,
            extra={"UV_CACHE_DIR": "/tmp/uv-cache"},
            wrap=lambda argv: confine_editable(argv, work, venv),
        )
        if done.returncode == 0:
            return {**env, "PATH": f"{venv / 'bin'}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    raise RuntimeError(f"install: {done.stderr[-400:]}")

    pkg = tmp_path / "oxide"

    root = tmp_path / "src"
    pkg = root / "oxide"
    pkg.mkdir(parents=True)
    (pkg / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (pkg / "__main__.py").write_text("print('tree-ok')\n", encoding="utf-8")
    done = subprocess.run(
        run.oxide_command("oxide-base", root), capture_output=True, text=True, check=False

    key, access, refresh = (
        "REDACTED",
        "access-token-0123",
        "refresh-token-0123",

    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    blob = json.dumps({"key": key, "access": access, "refresh": refresh})
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', ?)", (blob,))
    secrets = run.credential_values(db)
    assert key in secrets and access in secrets and refresh in secrets
    assert key not in run.confine.redact(f"used {key} and {access}", secrets)


def test_a_plain_credential_string_is_still_extracted(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    key = "REDACTED"
    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', ?)", (key,))

def test_git_on_agent_tree_is_confined(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}
    ran: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def confine_fn(argv: list[str], *, writable: Path, hide: object, net: bool) -> list[str]:
        seen["argv"] = list(argv)
        seen["net"] = net
        seen["writable"] = writable
        return ["bwrap", *map(str, argv)]

    def sh(*argv: str, **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        nonlocal ran
        ran = argv
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0)

    monkeypatch.setattr(run.confine, "confine", confine_fn)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "hidden", lambda: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(run.tasks, "sh", sh)
    base = tmp_path / "base"
    work = base / "work"
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    run.git_on_agent(base, "add", "-A", cwd=work)

    assert seen["net"] is False
    assert seen["writable"] == base

"""The agent's process is confined: no host secrets in its environment, the answers and other runs
hidden from its filesystem, and its kept traces free of the credential it used. Behaviour is
checked with the real bubblewrap where it is installed, and the rest with pure functions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
from collections.abc import Generator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Any

import pytest

SCRIPTS = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "agent_eval")
if SCRIPTS not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPTS)

confine: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("confine")
run: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("run")
tasks: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("tasks")

BWRAP = pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("bwrap") is None, reason="bubblewrap not installed")


@contextmanager
def home_scratch() -> Generator[Path, None, None]:
    """A directory under $HOME, not /tmp: confine mounts a tmpfs over /tmp, which would hide it
    for the wrong reason."""
    path = Path.home() / ".cache" / f"oxide-confine-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    path.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        yield path
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)


def test_the_agent_environment_holds_no_host_api_key(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "REDACTED")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GITHUB_TOKEN", "ghp_0123456789abcdef")
    env = confine.clean_env({"HOME": "/h"})
    assert "OPENAI_API_KEY" not in env and "GITHUB_TOKEN" not in env
    assert env["HOME"] == "/h"


def test_the_runner_passes_the_agent_only_the_clean_environment(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "REDACTED")
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}

    def fake_launch(
        command: list[str], cwd: Path, environment: dict[str, str], timeout: int
    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
        seen["environment"] = environment
        return "ok", ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "launch", fake_launch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(confine, "require", lambda: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "credentials", lambda *_: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "credential_values", lambda *_: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "forget_credentials", lambda *_: None)
    base = tmp_path / "base"
    (base / "work").mkdir(parents=True)
    run.agent("openai/m", "control", {"problem": "p"}, base, {"PATH": "/venv/bin"}, 1)
    assert "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" not in seen["environment"]


def test_without_bubblewrap_no_agent_is_started(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", "/nonexistent")
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="bubblewrap"):
        confine.confine(["true"], writable=Path("/tmp"), hide=(), net=False)


@BWRAP
def test_a_hidden_path_cannot_be_read_and_the_writable_one_can() -> None:
    with home_scratch() as root:
        answers = root / "answers"
        answers.mkdir()
        (answers / "gold.patch").write_text("secret", encoding="utf-8")
        work = root / "work"
        work.mkdir()
        read = confine.confine(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; open(sys.argv[1]).read()", answers / "gold.patch"],
            writable=work,
            hide=(answers,),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(read, capture_output=True).returncode != 0
        write = confine.confine(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; open(sys.argv[1], 'w').write('ok')", work / "f"],
            writable=work,
            hide=(answers,),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(write, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
        assert (work / "f").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "ok"


@BWRAP
def test_a_path_outside_the_writable_dir_cannot_be_written() -> None:
    with home_scratch() as root:
        work, other = root / "work", root / "other"
        work.mkdir()
        other.mkdir()
        argv = confine.confine(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; open(sys.argv[1], 'w')", other / "x"],
            writable=work,
            hide=(),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True).returncode != 0


def test_redaction_removes_a_secret_from_kept_text() -> None:
    key = "REDACTED"
    assert confine.redact(f"auth {key} done", [key]) == "auth [redacted] done"


def test_forgetting_credentials_empties_the_kept_copy(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', 'REDACTED')")
    run.forget_credentials(db)
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM credential").fetchone()[0] == 0


def test_forgetting_credentials_leaves_no_key_bytes_in_the_kept_file(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    key = "REDACTED"
    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', ?)", (key,))
    run.forget_credentials(db)
    assert key.encode() not in db.read_bytes()


def test_the_hidden_paths_cover_git_history_and_every_checkout_task_files(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repo, other = tmp_path / "repo", tmp_path / "other"
    git = ["git", "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@t"]
    subprocess.run([*git, "init", "-q", str(repo)], check=True)
    subprocess.run([*git, "-C", str(repo), "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "i"], check=True)
    subprocess.run([*git, "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "add", "-q", str(other)], check=True)
    hidden = {p.resolve() for p in run.hidden(other)}
    assert (repo / ".git").resolve() in hidden  # the shared history a linked checkout points at
    assert (repo / "fixtures" / "eval").resolve() in hidden
    assert (other / "fixtures" / "eval").resolve() in hidden


@BWRAP
def test_both_runners_host_credential_stores_are_unreadable_by_the_agent(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    with home_scratch() as root:
        work = root / "work"
        work.mkdir()
        stores = [
            root / "home" / ".codex" / "auth.json",
            root / "home" / ".local" / "share" / "opencode" / "opencode.db",
        ]
        for store in stores:
            store.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
            store.write_text("credential", encoding="utf-8")
        monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(root / "home"))
        for store in stores:
            probe = confine.confine(
                ["cat", str(store)], writable=work, hide=run.hidden(), net=False
            )
            assert subprocess.run(probe, capture_output=True).returncode != 0


@BWRAP
def test_the_answer_files_are_unreadable_by_a_confined_agent() -> None:
    with home_scratch() as work:
        probe = confine.confine(
            ["cat", str(tasks.TASKS)], writable=work, hide=run.hidden(), net=False
        )
        assert subprocess.run(probe, capture_output=True).returncode != 0


@BWRAP
def test_a_run_directory_under_the_hidden_cache_stays_writable() -> None:
    base = tasks.CACHE / "runs" / f"confine-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    base.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        write = confine.confine(
            ["sh", "-c", f"echo ok > {base / 'out.txt'}"],
            writable=base,
            hide=run.hidden(),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(write, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
        assert (base / "out.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() == "ok"
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)


def _symlink(link: Path, target: Path) -> None:
    try:
        link.symlink_to(target)
    except OSError:
        pytest.skip("symlinks unavailable")


def test_runtime_socket_mounts_hide_the_tree_and_keep_resolv(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = tmp_path / "run"
    sock = runtime / "libvirt" / "libvirt.sock"
    sock.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    sock.write_text("socket", encoding="utf-8")
    resolv = runtime / "systemd" / "resolve" / "stub-resolv.conf"
    resolv.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    resolv.write_text("nameserver 127.0.0.53\n", encoding="utf-8")
    link = tmp_path / "resolv.conf"
    _symlink(link, resolv)
    args = confine.socket_mounts([runtime], [link, tmp_path / "absent"])
    assert args[:2] == ["--tmpfs", str(runtime)]
    assert str(sock) not in args
    assert ("--dir", str(resolv.parent.parent)) in list(zip(args, args[1:], strict=True))
    assert args[-3:] == ["--ro-bind", str(resolv), str(resolv)]


def test_a_dangling_name_service_link_refuses_to_start(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = tmp_path / "run"
    runtime.mkdir()
